title: Earthquake bedside safety kit
summary: Prepare a small bedside set that reduces barefoot injuries, darkness, lost glasses, and delayed contact after night shaking.
steps: Place closed shoes, light, glasses, whistle, essential medicine card, and phone power where they can be reached without crossing broken glass.

title: Aftershock waiting-zone selection
summary: Choose a temporary waiting place that avoids façades, glass, power lines, unstable walls, traffic, and blocked emergency access.
steps: After the initial shaking, account for people and move only by a route that does not pass obvious falling-object, gas, fire, or electrical hazards.

title: Post-earthquake stair and exit check
summary: Use a cautious visual exit check so people do not rush into damaged stairs, lifts, falling debris, smoke, or gas.
steps: Do not use lifts; inspect the route from a safe position and keep everyone away when cracks, movement, smoke, water, sparks, or gas odour are present.

title: Earthquake cabinet and falling-object control
summary: Reduce preventable indoor injuries by moving heavy items low and securing unstable furniture, shelves, tanks, and cabinet doors.
steps: Prioritise objects above beds, exits, seating, children’s areas, and utility controls, then test that the fix does not create a new sharp, trip, or fire hazard.

title: Earthquake re-entry boundary card
summary: Create a visible stop card that prevents casual re-entry into a visibly damaged or officially restricted building.
steps: Treat new cracks, shifted supports, falling material, gas odour, fire, sparks, flooding, jammed exits, or official restriction as no-entry conditions.
